newsitem.title: USA: CBOT rice ends lower on weak cash, deliveries.
newsitem.headline: CBOT rice ends lower on weak cash, deliveries.

text.p: CBOT rice futures ended lower Wednesday, pressured by weakness in the cash market and prospects for more deliveries against the March, traders said.
"We're seeing more warehouse receipts that will probably be delivered against the March," a floor trader said.
Cash prices in the country were weak but traders noted some upcoming tenders could put a spark back into the market. Costa Rica will tender on March 19 for 30,000 tonnes optional origin rough rice.
Exporters said the sale would likely be U.S. and or Argentine origin.
Bulls continued to watch rains in the U.S. south which threatened to delay rice plantings.
"We're all sitting here watching the rain fall in Texas," a trader said. "They're getting to be late in planting in Texas and also in Louisiana."
Traders expected weekly exports to be below 15,000 tonnes in Thursday's USDA export sales report due at 0730 CST.
Rice ended 15-1/2 to two cents lower, with May off 15 at $11.61 per cwt.
Volume was estimated by CBOT at 600 lots, compared with Tuesday's actual volume of 542 lots.
